Who the videos are for

Four truckers. Four reasons to reach out.

1

The new authority

Just got a DOT and MC number and needs primary liability and cargo before the first load.

"What insurance do I need to start running?"
2

The renewal shock

An owner-operator or small fleet whose premium jumped at renewal with no clear reason why.

"Why did my truck insurance go up so much?"
3

The growing fleet

Adding trucks and drivers, and outgrowing a one-size policy and an agent who doesn't know trucking.

"How do I insure my next five trucks?"
4

The non-renewed

Dropped by a carrier or carrying a tough loss run, and needs someone who can shop the whole market.

"My carrier dropped me. Now what?"

Every one of them is already asking these questions on Google, YouTube and AI tools like ChatGPT. We make sure Resolute is the answer they find.

06
Four kinds of truckers, each with a question they're already searching. The new authority who needs coverage before the first load. The renewal shock, whose premium jumped. The growing fleet, adding trucks and outgrowing their current agent. And the non-renewed, dropped by a carrier and needing someone who can shop 15-plus carriers. Each question becomes a short video, and each video points to one next step: book a quote call with Resolute.

Where truckers look first now

New carriers ask ChatGPT before they ask anyone. Who does it name?

AI assistant · ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, GoogleExample
I just got my MC number in Arkansas and I'm buying my first truck. Who should I talk to about primary liability and cargo insurance?

New authorities usually pay the most, so it's worth working with an agency that specializes in trucking and can shop several carriers. Owner-operators often mention:

Resolute Insurance Group (Little Rock) has a team dedicated to trucking insurance and shops coverage across 15+ A-rated carriers.
SourcesYouTube · "New authority? 3 mistakes"Trucker forum threadDispatcher's blogresoluteinsurancegroup.com
1

It gives one answer, not ten links

An AI names two or three agencies. If Resolute isn't one of them, the trucker never sees you.

2

It trusts what others say about you

The AI builds its answer from videos, articles, forums and reviews across the web, not from your own ads.

3

The trucker arrives already sold

When they call, the AI has already told them you're the people to talk to. That's an inbound call, not a cold one.

10
[Click 1: the answer appears. Click 2: last point.] More and more, a new carrier types the question into ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity or Google, which now answers at the top of the page. The AI doesn't hand back ten links. It names two or three agencies. So the question for Resolute is: when a new authority in Arkansas asks, are you one of the names? The AI builds that answer from what other people say about you across the web, not from your ads. This answer is an example of what we're aiming for, not a real result today.
How creators put Resolute in AI answers

Claiming your listing is step one. Being talked about is the rest.

Step one · we do it in week one

Claim Resolute in ChatGPT's business hub

Name, address, phone, licensed states, lines of coverage, hours. It makes sure the AI has your facts right.

Said out loud, saved as text

Truckers, dispatchers and accountants all use the same phrases: trucking insurance, new authority, 15+ A-rated carriers. The AI learns to connect them to you.

4

Posted where AI looks

YouTube, podcasts, trucking forums, industry blogs and reviews, each linking back to your booking page.

5

We check every month

12
QLC, Qualified Lead Count: trucking operations in your licensed states that booked a quote call and need coverage now or at renewal. CPL: what each of those truckers cost to bring in. And because every lead is tracked from first view to closed policy, we can tell you what it costs to win a customer, not just a lead. At kickoff we agree the states, what counts as qualified and bound, and where leads should go in your lead capture system. On top of that, a monthly AI check of 25 trucker questions.
Week to week

Test small. Back the winners.

1

Film

Your agents film from our 10 scripts, and we recruit the first trucker creators and industry voices.

2

Post to followers

Creators post to their own followers, and Resolute shares with past clients, testing the content first.

3

Read the response

Watch time, shares, comments and saves. Change one thing at a time: trucker type, message or face.

Back the winners

A booking page on the new .com: a longer video and a short form. How many trucks, new or active authority, when do you renew?

6

Route to the bullpen

The lead lands in your lead capture system, goes to an agent, and we track it to a bound policy.

Your agents don't disappear

Keep the bullpen. Change who's on the other end.

A producer's day today
  1. Work a list of new authorities
  2. Dial, leave a voicemail, dial again
  3. Explain who Resolute is to someone six agents already called
  4. The pipeline leaves when the producer does
With the lead engine
  1. Start with truckers who booked a quote call
  2. Call people who already watched your agents on video
  3. Cold dials last, and fewer of them
  4. Every lead stays with Resolute, tracked to a bound policy

Same team, same carriers. Less chasing, less turnover, more time with truckers who want the help.

15
[Click 1: the new day. Click 2: the takeaway.] We're not replacing the bullpen. We're changing the order of their day. First, truckers who booked a quote call. Then people who've already seen your agents on video, so the call isn't cold. Cold dials last, and fewer of them. And because every lead comes through Resolute's system, nothing walks out the door when someone leaves. A seat that's fed with warm leads is also an easier seat to keep filled.
